content:
oli: Quick check — I'm seeing auth headers dropped when running the Node/TS SDK in Vercel Edge (ESM build + Vite). Anyone run into this? PR 621 touches retry logic so want to make sure nothing else regressed.

maya: yes, saw similar a week ago. In our case it was Vite optimizing the SDK into the bundle and the edge runtime shimming fetch differently. Marking the package as external fixed it for us.

frank: can you paste the import + vite/next config?

oli: sure — simplified snippet from the app:

```
import Redwood from 'redwood-js';

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-small', prompt });
```

vite config currently has nothing special for redwood-js. Next is an edge route (export const runtime = 'edge').

maya: two things we did:
1) in next.config.js for Next/Vercel edge, add webpack externals or using Vite: ssr.noExternal: ['redwood-js'] (or the opposite depending on the bundler).
2) ensure the auth header is set inside the edge handler sync path — some builds inline env replacements and they disappear at runtime if bundled/transformed.

sam: small reminder: ESM default export interop can differ. If your SDK publishes both CJS+ESM, try `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-js'` or `import Redwood from 'redwood-js/dist/esm'` in a quick repro.

frank: also check streaming + retry interactions — if a retry happens the edge runtime might re-run initializer code and re-create streams. We added an idempotency header `x-redwood-idempotency-key` for the retry path so retries are single-shot server-side.

oli: interesting — PR 621 changes client retry backoff but doesn't set idempotency header for stream retries. That could explain double-processing. I'll add idempotency support.

maya: and for Vite specifically, try this in vite.config.ts:

```
export default defineConfig({
  ssr: { noExternal: ['redwood-js'] },
  optimizeDeps: { exclude: ['redwood-js'] }
});
```

that kept our edge bundles from mangling the runtime fetch shim.

sam: one more gotcha — when targeting edge, avoid relying on global process.env at runtime. Bundle-time inlining will substitute values; prefer passing secrets via platform env or edge secrets (Vercel edge envs) and use them via globalThis.__REDWOOD_ENV or explicit fetch header construction.

oli: thanks — I'll try marking external + add idempotency header for streaming retries. If that doesn't fix, I'll push a tiny repro to the branch.

devex-bot: FYI — documented recommended Next/Vite config in /docs/sdk/edge-deployments.md (PR 534).

frank: ping me on the PR once you add the repro, I'll do a quick run on Vercel. :thumbsup:
